_README: EQLS Auras is Shara's project. Shara has creative and production control over it and her copy reaches this file through the owner. NOTHING IN HERE MAY BE WRITTEN BY A BUILD SESSION. lede and body[0] are her Pitch section from HIGHLIGHTS.md, verbatim, replacing text from the product's first version that was still live on launch day and described roughly a hundredth of what it now does. Faithful transport preserved an obsolete claim perfectly, which is why this file names its source: point it at the current one when she updates it.
name: EQLS Auras
lede: Stop alt-tabbing to check your buffs. EQLS Auras reads your EverQuest Legends log and shows a countdown overlay on top of the game.
body: EQLS Auras watches your log while you play and puts a click-through overlay on screen with a timer for every buff you’re running. Build as many overlays as you want, put them where you want, give them sounds. Point an aura at any line in your log, not just buffs the app knows. It hides when you tab out of EQ and comes back when you tab in. It tracks your weekly raid lockouts, which EQ never prints.

It reads files the client already has: the log it writes as you play, your spellbook, and the game’s own spell icons. It does not read or alter the game’s memory, inject code into it, or send it input. It fetches its typeface from Google each time it launches, which discloses your IP address to Google; beyond that it sends nothing — no telemetry, no analytics, no update check. That fetch is the main window only: the overlay drawn over the game requests nothing at all.
The idea is WeakAuras’. The code is not: a from-scratch implementation for EverQuest Legends, sharing no code and no trigger format with it, and neither affiliated with nor endorsed by its authors.

Each renders in a fixed 16:9 slot, so adding one moves no layout. An animated GIF is treated as an image and is not motion-gated; prefer a video for anything long.

band.alt: The EQLS Auras overlay running over the game, buff icons across the top of the screen each counting down its own remaining time.
subs: Add overlays and put them where you want. Point an aura at any line in your log, not just buffs the app knows. It shows what you have landed on each groupmate, skins your action bar, routes you across the map, and tracks the weekly raid lockouts EQ never prints. One key hides the lot.

It reads files the client already has: the log it writes as you play, your spellbook, and the game’s own spell icons. It does not read or alter the game’s memory, inject code into it, or send it input. No telemetry, no analytics, no update check.
band.foot: Free. It finds your EverQuest install on its own. Windows SmartScreen warns about an unknown publisher — More info, then Run anyway.
